question:
For $D=\begin{vmatrix}x & 1 & 2\\2 & x & 1\\1 & 2 & x\end{vmatrix}$:

(a) Expand $D$ and obtain a cubic polynomial in $x$.

(b) Factorise the polynomial completely.

(c) Hence, determine all values of $x$ for which $D=0$.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=x\begin{vmatrix}x & 1\\2 & x\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & x\end{vmatrix}+2\begin{vmatrix}2 & x\\1 & 2\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=x(x^2-2)-(2x-1)+2(4-x)$$
$$D=x^3-2x-2x+1+8-2x$$
$$D=x^3-6x+9$$

(b)
Since $x=-3$ is a zero of $x^3-6x+9$, $(x+3)$ is a factor. Dividing gives
$$x^3-6x+9=(x+3)(x^2-3x+3)$$
Thus, the required factorisation is
$$D=(x+3)(x^2-3x+3)$$

(c)
For $D=0$,
$$x+3=0\quad\text{or}\quad x^2-3x+3=0$$
The discriminant of the quadratic factor is
$$(-3)^2-4(1)(3)=9-12=-3<0$$
Therefore, the quadratic factor has no real zero. Hence, the only real value is
$$x=-3$$

options.D:
(a) $D=x^3-6x+9$
(b) $D=(x+3)(x^2-3x+3)$
(c) The only real value for which $D=0$ is $x=-3$
